title: Gocast — apps, terminal and clipboard on one key
desc: Gocast is a free, open-source launcher for the Mac. Press ⌘Space to open any app, ⌃` for a drop-down terminal, ⌃⌘V for clipboard history, and do math right in search.
h1a: One key. Apps and terminal, right there.
h1b: Your hands stay on the keyboard.
sub: Gocast is a free, open-source launcher for the Mac. Opening an app, dropping down a terminal, finding something you copied, doing a quick sum: each is one shortcut away.
req: Free · Open source · macOS 13 or later · Apple silicon
hero_alt: The Gocast search panel, with your usual apps and presets under the search field

features.title: Type a few letters. Your app is open.
features.text: English names, Chinese names and pinyin all work. The apps you use most come first and are listed the moment the panel opens, so often you don’t type at all.
features.alt: Searching: typing chat puts WeChat first, with ChatGPT below it

features.title: A terminal drops down from the top.
features.text: It floats above every app, and hiding it stops nothing. A preset remembers which command to run in which folder, like pi in my-app. When the command ends, the tab becomes a plain terminal and you keep typing.
features.alt: The floating terminal dropped down from the top, with two tabs, one of them a preset

features.title: Everything you copied is still here.
features.text: Text, links, images and files, with thumbnails for screenshots. Press ↵ to paste into the app you were in, and pin the ones you use often. It stays on this Mac, and passwords from password managers are never kept.
features.alt: Clipboard history with text, links and images in the list and a picture previewed on the right

features.title: Do the math right in search.
features.text: Type (12+8)*3, 10 ft in m or 100 usd in jpy and the answer is on top. Press ↵ to copy it. Exchange rates update once a day from central bank reference rates.
features.alt: Typing 100 usd in jpy in search, with the converted answer on top

features.title: Give each favorite app its own shortcut.
features.text: Set a shortcut for any app or preset and press it anywhere: it opens the app, brings it forward, or hides it if it’s already in front. Find it in Settings › Shortcuts, or select it in the search panel and press ⌘K.
features.alt: Settings › Shortcuts: Gocast’s own three shortcuts on top, then every app and preset, a few already set

pv.h: It all stays on your Mac.
pv.p: Gocast has no account and sends none of your information anywhere. Your presets, settings, clipboard history and what you open all stay on this Mac. It goes online for only two things, and neither carries anything you typed or copied:

items.v: from GitHub, about once a day; when there’s a newer version, it downloads in the background.

pv.note: Both can be turned off in Settings › General.

close_h: Free, open source, and ready once it’s installed.
s_lede: Gocast is a free launcher for the Mac: apps, a drop-down terminal and clipboard history, each on one key.
s_contact: Report a problem or ask a question in GitHub Issues. We usually reply within a few days. For a security problem, don’t open a public issue: use “Report a vulnerability” on the repository’s Security tab.

faq.a: Spotlight uses ⌘Space by default, so Gocast starts on ⌥⇧Space. Turn off “Show Spotlight search” in System Settings › Keyboard › Keyboard Shortcuts › Spotlight and Gocast switches to ⌘Space on its own. Or pick any shortcut in Gocast’s Settings › Shortcuts.

To paste into another app, Gocast presses ⌘V for you, and macOS asks you to turn on Gocast in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility first. Until then, Return copies and you press ⌘V yourself.

faq.q: Which Macs does it run on?
faq.a: macOS 13 or later on Apple silicon. Intel support is planned.

Quit Gocast from its menu bar icon and move it to the Trash, or run:
curl -fsSL https://github.com/xcc3641/gocast/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh -s -- --uninstall
Your presets, settings and clipboard history stay in ~/Library/Application Support/com.hugo.gocast/; delete that folder to remove them too.

p_lede: Gocast has no account and collects nothing about you. This page says exactly what it keeps and when it goes online.

p_sections.text: Nothing. Gocast has no account, no analytics, no ads and no crash reporting. We never receive anything you type, copy or run.

Your presets, settings and clipboard history are files in ~/Library/Application Support/com.hugo.gocast/, readable only by your Mac user. They are never uploaded. Clipboard history is kept as plain files, not encrypted. Gocast also keeps a record of what you open from search and which search led to it, so the things you use come first. That record is a plain file in the same folder; each search is kept for 17 days, and turning clipboard history off does not touch it. Passwords copied from password managers are never kept, and you can choose apps whose copies are never kept.

Only twice, and neither request carries anything you typed or copied:
  • Checking for updates, from the Gocast project on GitHub, about once a day; when there is a newer version, it downloads it in the background. Turn it off with Settings › General › Check for updates automatically.
  • Exchange rates for the calculator, from Frankfurter (frankfurter.dev), once a day. Turn it off with Settings › General › Calculate in search.
GitHub and Frankfurter see the request like any website sees a visit, such as your IP address, under their own privacy policies. Gocast sends them nothing else.
Gocast shares no data with anyone. The only outside services it contacts are the two above.

Clipboard history is kept for one month by default; change it in Settings › Clipboard (1 day to forever). Pinned items don’t expire. Clear History removes it at once. To delete everything, quit Gocast and delete ~/Library/Application Support/com.hugo.gocast/.
Turn off clipboard history in Settings › Clipboard, and update checks or exchange rates in Settings › General, at any time. Nothing has to be sent to us, because nothing ever was.
